I have a real carry gun (P250 .40) and a tiny gun, and I carry the second when I can't carry the first.

Tiny guns are a pain - invariably harder and slower to shoot, and always underpowered. Their only saving grace is that when it comes time to choose between a tiny gun and no gun, a tiny gun is a whole lot better than no gun. They only exist for those times when anything else would just be too big to take along.

So my advice is to meet the 'tiny' requirement first. If you won't ever find yourself in a position where the little glock is just too big to carry, then get the glock or something like it. But if your realize that there are times when you'd carry the ruger, but you'd leave the glock at home, then the ruger is the better choice.

You might be able to improve it with one of those slip-on rubber grip sleeves. They add a little thickness and a lot of grippiness, and that helps more than you might think. (Use plenty of oil and they are not too hard to put on).

There are some guns between the glock and ruger in size that might serve you better - the colt mustang and Sig's 938 come to mind, and Kahr offers some little stuff too. The RM380 is yet another option.
